reference.title: Environment variable reference
reference.shortdesc: Every setting of , with its default and the rules it is checked against at start-up.

ul.li: All settings are environment variables; nothing is baked into the image. Give the web service and the worker the same values.
Every command (serve, worker, migrate, seed) checks the whole set at start-up and refuses to start with a list of every problem.
An empty value counts as unset. So does an unresolved reference variable on Railway.
Flags are on when set to 1 or true, and off otherwise.
The web editor has its own settings, listed in .

Some settings can instead be changed by staff in the admin console (sign-in, the GitHub connection, editor links). A variable that is set always wins over the console, which then shows the setting read-only. See .

property.propdesc: Postgres connection string, such as postgres://opend:secret@db:5432/opend.

Where readers reach the site. Must be a URL; a trailing slash is removed. It is the OIDC callback base, the audience of embed tokens, and the base of absolute links in PDFs and the JSON API. When it starts with https://, cookies are marked Secure.
Port to listen on: an integer from 0 to 65535.
Interface to listen on.

Signs session cookies. At least 32 characters. Changing it signs every reader out. Without OPEND_SECRET_KEY, the key that seals stored secrets is derived from it, so changing it also makes those secrets unreadable until they are entered again.

Seals the secrets the admin console stores (client secrets, the GitHub App's private key and webhook secret) with AES-256-GCM. At least 32 characters. Set it to rotate SESSION_SECRET freely; give the web, worker and editor services the same value. See .
With production, the server refuses to start with OPEND_DEV_LOGIN, and sign-in refuses an http:// OIDC issuer.
The repository the site serves, as owner/name, when more than one is registered. Without it, the site works only while exactly one repository is registered.
Bearer token for the admin API. At least 24 characters. Without it the admin API does not exist. The admin console at /admin does not need it: staff readers sign in.

The secret set on the repository's or GitHub App's webhook. Without it, the webhook secret of the app connected in the admin console is used, and without either, /webhooks/github answers 503. In managed hosting, the control plane re-signs forwarded deliveries with this value.

The GitHub App's id, for private repositories and commit statuses. Set together with GITHUB_APP_PRIVATE_KEY. Without it, Connect GitHub in the admin console creates and stores an app instead (). Not together with OPEND_GITHUB_BROKER_URL.
The App's private key, PEM, PKCS#1 as GitHub issues it or PKCS#8. Literal \n sequences are turned into line breaks, so the key fits on one line. Set together with GITHUB_APP_ID.
API base URL, for GitHub Enterprise Server, such as https://github.example.com/api/v3. Must be a URL.

Managed hosting only: the control plane's token broker, such as https://control.example/broker/v1. The worker, poller and editor get installation tokens from it (read for builds, write for the editor and commit statuses) instead of a GitHub App of their own, and the admin console's repository picker lists what it returns. Set by the hosting provider, together with OPEND_GITHUB_BROKER_SECRET.
This instance's bearer token for the broker. At least 16 characters.
Managed hosting: the shared GitHub App's installation page, such as https://github.com/apps/opend/installations/new. The admin console's Connect GitHub button links to it.
The OpenID Connect issuer URL. Requires OIDC_CLIENT_ID and OIDC_CLIENT_SECRET.
The client id registered with the provider.
The client secret.
Scopes to request, space-separated. Keep email: readers are matched by verified email.
How the sign-in page names the OIDC provider: Sign in with name. At most 60 characters. With GitHub, the button shows GitHub's mark.

property.propvalue: key (github when the display name is GitHub)
property.propdesc: The OIDC button's icon: key or github. Managed hosting signs readers in with GitHub through its own OIDC provider and sets github.
Adds Sign in with GitHub. The client id of the GitHub App (or an OAuth App). The same name and value as the web editor's, so one GitHub App serves both. Set together with GITHUB_OAUTH_CLIENT_SECRET.
The matching client secret.
Where GitHub sign-in sends readers, for GitHub Enterprise Server. Must be a URL.

An org slug. A GitHub user with write, maintain or admin access to the site's repository, whose primary email GitHub has verified and no reader uses yet, becomes a reader of this org on first sign-in. Needs GitHub sign-in and GITHUB_APP_ID, and the repository registered with its installation id. The org must exist.
Flag. Readers added by OPEND_GITHUB_COLLABORATOR_ORG are staff: they see everything, conditions marked. Needs OPEND_GITHUB_COLLABORATOR_ORG.

Flag. Lists every registered reader under Demo readers on the sign-in page, where anyone can sign in as any of them, for evaluation without an identity provider. Refused when NODE_ENV=production. Staff can turn it off (and on again) in the admin console, but never on without this flag.

The web editor's address, such as https://edit.docs.example. Signed-in readers get an Edit this page link on topic pages, opening the topic's source file in the editor. The editor still decides who may edit. Must be a URL. Without it, the address set in the admin console (Editor) is used.

Flag. Adds View source on GitHub to topic pages of a repository cloned from https://github.com, pointing at the built commit. Every viewer sees it, anonymous visitors of a public site too, so turn it on only when the repository is public or every reader may read it.
Folder for images, themes and PDFs when no bucket is configured. Web and worker must share it.
Bucket name. Setting it switches to S3-compatible storage, and then S3_ENDPOINT, S3_ACCESS_KEY_ID and S3_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY are required too: all four or none.
Service URL, such as https://s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com. Must be a URL.
Access key id.
Secret access key.
Region. Most S3-compatible services accept auto.
Flag. Address the bucket as /<bucket>/<key> instead of <bucket>.<host>, for MinIO and similar services.
Prepended to every key, such as opend/, to share a bucket.
Shared secret host apps sign embed tokens with. At least 32 characters. Set together with OPEND_EMBED_ORIGINS; without both, embedding is off.
Comma-separated origins allowed to frame the help panel and call the JSON API, such as https://console.example.com,http://localhost:5173. Each must be http or https with no path or trailing slash.

section.title: Analytics and feedback
section.p: See Docs analytics and reader feedback for what is recorded.

property.propdesc: On unless set to 0, false, off or no. Off records no page views, searches or feedback and hides the "Was this page helpful?" form. The analytics admin routes still answer with what was recorded before.

Days to keep analytics rows: a whole number from 1 to 3650. The worker deletes older rows when it starts and every six hours after, even with analytics off. opend-server purge-analytics does it on demand.

section.title: PDF printing
section.p: Read by the PDF renderer when it first starts Chromium.

property.propvalue: the browser Playwright installed (the image sets /usr/bin/chromium)
property.propdesc: Path of the Chromium binary that prints PDFs.
Set to exactly 1 to run Chromium with its own sandbox, where the runtime allows the namespaces it needs.

section.title: Docker Compose only
section.p: POSTGRES_PASSWORD (default opend) and OPEND_PORT (default 3000) are read by deploy/docker-compose.yml, not by the server.
